skills.grammarTip: Bosnian distinguishes informal address (ti) from formal or plural address (vi): 'Kako si?' (asking one person you're informal with) vs 'Kako ste?' (formal, or speaking to more than one person). The word 'molim' does double duty — it means 'please' when asking for something, and 'you're welcome' when replying to 'hvala'.

skills.title: Dnevna rutina
skills.grammarTip: Reflexive verbs pair a verb with the short pronoun 'se', which stays the same for every person: 'buditi se' (to wake oneself up) → ja se budim, ti se budiš, on/ona se budi, mi se budimo, vi se budite, oni se bude. 'Se' usually comes right after the verb, but jumps in front of it in questions: 'Kada se budiš?' (When do you wake up?). Everyday routine verbs like raditi, učiti and večerati follow the regular present-tense pattern: radim, radiš, radi, radimo, radite, rade.

to leave / to go (to work, school)

skills.title: Hrana i piće
skills.grammarTip: The accusative case marks the direct object — what you eat or drink. Feminine nouns ending in -a change that ending to -u: voda → Pijem vodu (I drink water), kafa → Pijem kafu. Masculine and neuter nouns for inanimate things keep the same form as the nominative: hljeb → Jedem hljeb, meso → Jedem meso. The verbs 'jesti' (to eat) and 'piti' (to drink) always take their object in the accusative: Šta jedeš? Jedem sir. Šta piješ? Pijem sok.

skills.title: Kupovina
skills.grammarTip: When you talk about quantities and prices, the noun that follows goes into the genitive case. After the numbers 2, 3 and 4 use the genitive singular: dva kilograma, tri eura; from 5 upward, and after quantity words like kilogram and litar, use the genitive plural: pet eura, kilogram krompira (a kilo of potatoes), litar mlijeka (a liter of milk). To ask a price, use 'Koliko košta...?' (How much does... cost?) — the thing being priced itself stays in the nominative: Koliko košta hljeb?

skills.title: Vrijeme i dani
skills.grammarTip: To say 'on' a day of the week, Bosnian uses 'u' + the accusative case: u ponedjeljak, u utorak, u četvrtak and u petak look identical to the nominative (masculine nouns), but feminine day names change their ending: srijeda → u srijedu, subota → u subotu, nedjelja → u nedjelju. Weather is described with 'Vani je...' (It's... outside) followed by a fixed adverbial form that never changes: Vani je sunčano, vani je hladno, vani je toplo. Note that 'vrijeme' means both 'time' and 'weather' — context tells you which.

units.title: Grad i kretanje
units.theme: Giving and following directions, using public transport, talking about the past, and describing hobbies and free-time activities.

skills.title: Upute i pravci
skills.grammarTip: To give directions, use the imperative: 'skrenuti' (to turn) becomes skreni (informal) or skrenite (formal / plural) — Skreni lijevo! (Turn left!) Skrenite desno! (Turn right!). Many place prepositions — iza (behind), pored (next to), blizu (near), između (between), kod (at/by) — govern the genitive case: iza semafora (behind the traffic light), pored raskrsnice (next to the intersection), kod stanice (at the station).

skills.title: Prijevoz
skills.grammarTip: The locative case answers 'where?' and always follows 'u' or 'na'. Masculine and neuter nouns typically add -u: autobus → u autobusu (on the bus), voz → u vozu (on the train), aerodrom → na aerodromu (at the airport). Some nouns pair with 'na' by convention even though they aren't open surfaces — na stanici (at the station) — while enclosed vehicles usually take 'u': u autobusu, u tramvaju, u taksiju.

skills.title: Prošlo vrijeme
skills.grammarTip: The perfekt (past tense) is formed with the present tense of 'biti' (to be) plus the l-participle of the main verb, which changes for gender: masculine ends in -o, feminine in -la. 'Raditi' (to work) → (ja) radio sam / radila sam (I worked); 'ići' (to go) → išao sam / išla sam; 'vidjeti' (to see) → vidio sam / vidjela sam. In speech the auxiliary 'sam' usually comes right after the participle: Jučer sam radio. Prošle sedmice sam putovao u Sarajevo.

units.title: Posao i obrazovanje
units.theme: Workplace and career vocabulary with the dative case, school and university life with relative clauses, health and the doctor's office with modal verbs, and expressing and defending opinions with subordinate clauses.

skills.title: Posao
skills.grammarTip: The dative case marks the indirect object — the person 'to' or 'for' whom something happens — and follows verbs like reći, dati, pomoći, and pisati. Masculine nouns add -u (šef → šefu), nouns ending in -a like kolega/kolegica change to -i (kolega → kolegi, kolegica → kolegici), and neuter nouns add -u (dijete → djetetu). 'Pomogao sam kolegici sa izvještajem' — I helped my colleague (f.) with the report.

skills.title: Obrazovanje
skills.grammarTip: The relative pronoun koji (who/which) agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to, but its case depends on its role inside the clause: 'Profesor koji predaje historiju' (nominative, subject), 'Predmet koji najviše volim' (accusative, object), 'Fakultet na kojem studiram' (locative, after a preposition). Feminine forms are koja/koju; neuter is koje.

skills.title: Zdravlje
skills.grammarTip: Trebati, morati, and moći are the three core modal verbs. Morati expresses strict obligation ('moram uzeti lijek' — I must take medicine); moći expresses ability or permission ('mogu li zakazati termin?' — can I book an appointment?); trebati expresses need and can be personal ('trebam ići kod ljekara' — I need to go to the doctor) or impersonal with the dative ('treba mi lijek' — I need medicine, literally 'medicine is needed to me').

skills.grammarTip: To state an opinion, follow mislim da / smatram da (I think/believe that) with a full subordinate clause that has its own subject and verb: 'Mislim da je ovo dobra ideja' (I think that this is a good idea). To agree or disagree, use slažem se / ne slažem se sa + instrumental: 'Slažem se s tobom' (I agree with you).

units.title: Putovanja i mediji
units.theme: Travel bookings and directions abroad with the future tense, internet and news vocabulary with comparatives and superlatives, future intentions and plans, and real versus hypothetical conditional sentences.

skills.title: Putovanja
skills.grammarTip: The future tense combines clitic forms of htjeti (ću, ćeš, će, ćemo, ćete, će) with the infinitive: 'Ja ću putovati', or, when the infinitive comes right before it, the merged form 'putovaću' (putovati + ću). The clitic cannot open a sentence — say 'Sutra ću putovati', not 'Ću putovati sutra'. Negation is a single word — neću, nećeš, neće… + infinitive — and never merges: 'Neću putovati.'

exercises.promptEn: Tomorrow I will travel to Sarajevo.
What does the word 'prtljag' mean?

skills.title: Mediji i tehnologija
skills.grammarTip: Comparatives are usually formed by adding -iji/-ji/-eći to the adjective stem (brz → brži, zanimljiv → zanimljiviji) and are followed by od + noun, or nego + clause, to mean 'than'. Superlatives simply add naj- to the comparative form: brži → najbrži (fastest). A handful of common adjectives are irregular: dobar → bolji → najbolji (good/better/best), loš → gori → najgori (bad/worse/worst).

skills.title: Planovi i budućnost
skills.grammarTip: Namjeravati and planirati (+ infinitive) express intentions and plans: 'Namjeravam upisati fakultet' (I intend to enroll in college). After temporal conjunctions like kad/čim (when/as soon as) that point to a future event, Bosnian keeps the subordinate verb in the present tense rather than the future: 'Kad završim školu, naći ću posao' (When I finish school, I'll find a job) — never 'kad ću završiti'.

skills.title: Uslovne rečenice
skills.grammarTip: Real conditions use ako + present tense in both clauses, with the main clause often in the future: 'Ako imam vremena, doći ću' (If I have time, I'll come). Unreal or hypothetical conditions use the conditional mood (bih/bi/bismo/biste + l-participle) in both clauses, typically introduced by kad bi(h): 'Kad bih imao više novca, kupio bih kuću' (If I had more money, I would buy a house).

units.title: Društvo i kultura
units.theme: Upper-intermediate discussion of social issues, environmental challenges, arts and culture, and national history and tradition — building nuanced vocabulary, subordinate clauses, verbal aspect, and passive constructions.

skills.title: Društvo
skills.grammarTip: Na B2 nivou rečenice se sve češće povezuju zavisnim veznicima poput 'iako', 'budući da' i 's obzirom na to da', umjesto nizanja kratkih nezavisnih rečenica: 'Iako je nezaposlenost visoka, mladi ostaju optimistični.' Formalni bosanski jezik također često pretvara glagole u apstraktne imenice (nominalizacija): 'odlučiti' postaje 'odluka', 'promijeniti' postaje 'promjena' — postupak tipičan za novinski i akademski stil.

skills.title: Okoliš
skills.grammarTip: Pasivna rečenica sa 'se' opisuje radnju bez isticanja ko je vrši i vrlo je česta u govoru o okolišu: 'Šume se sijeku brže nego što rastu.' / 'Otpad se mora reciklirati.' Ovo se razlikuje od pravog pasiva s 'biti' + trpni pridjev ('Šuma je posječena'), koji naglašava rezultat radnje, dok se-pasiv opisuje opću, ponavljanu praksu.

skills.title: Kultura i umjetnost
skills.grammarTip: Bosanski glagoli dolaze u parovima prema vidu: nesvršeni glagol opisuje radnju u toku ili radnju koja se ponavlja ('slikati' — slikao je cijeli mjesec), a svršeni glagol opisuje završenu, jednokratnu radnju ('naslikati' — naslikao je sliku prošle sedmice). Isto vrijedi za 'pisati/napisati', 'gledati/pogledati', 'čitati/pročitati' — izbor vida mijenja značenje rečenice, ne samo vrijeme.

skills.title: Historija i tradicija
skills.grammarTip: U pripovijedanju o prošlosti, posebno u narodnim pričama i legendama, pored svakodnevnog perfekta ('je došao') ponekad se sreću i knjiški prošli oblici: aorist ('dođe' — kratko, jednokratno svršeno) i imperfekt ('bijaše', 'življaše' — radnja koja je trajala). Na B2 nivou dovoljno je prepoznati ove oblike u tekstu, iako se u svakodnevnom govoru gotovo isključivo koristi perfekt.

units.title: Apstraktne teme
units.theme: Abstract and opinion-based discourse spanning politics and economy, emotions and relationships, hypothetical wishes, and everyday idioms — reinforcing formal connectors, reflexive/reciprocal verbs, the conditional mood, and fixed expressions.

skills.title: Politika i ekonomija
skills.grammarTip: Formalni govor o politici i ekonomiji oslanja se na vezničke izraze koji jasno pokazuju logiku argumenta: 'dakle' (zaključak), 'stoga' (posljedica), 's druge strane' (suprotnost) i 'međutim' (kontrast). Na primjer: 'Inflacija raste, stoga vlada najavljuje reformu poreza. S druge strane, mnogi građani strahuju od korupcije.' Ovakvi veznici obilježavaju formalniji registar nego svakodnevni razgovor.

skills.title: Emocije i odnosi
skills.grammarTip: Povratni glagoli sa 'se' opisuju stanja i radnje usmjerene na samog sebe ('osjećati se dobro', 'zaljubiti se'), dok recipročni glagoli sa 'se' opisuju uzajamnu radnju dvoje ili više ljudi ('razumjeti se', 'posvađati se', 'pomiriti se'). U oba slučaja 'se' je obavezan dio glagola i ne prevodi se doslovno na engleski.

skills.title: Izražavanje želja
skills.grammarTip: Kondicional se gradi od radnog glagolskog pridjeva i pomoćnog glagola 'biti' u posebnom obliku (bih, bi, bi, bismo, biste, bi): 'Volio bih putovati.' Za izražavanje želje ili namjere česta je i konstrukcija sa 'da': 'Želim da naučim bosanski.' U hipotetičkim rečenicama kondicional se koristi i u glavnoj i u zavisnoj rečenici: 'Kad bih imao vremena, putovao bih više.'

skills.title: Idiomi i izrazi
skills.grammarTip: Idiomi su ustaljeni izrazi čije se značenje ne može izvesti iz pojedinačnih riječi — 'praviti se Englez' nema nikakve veze s Engleskom, već znači 'pretvarati se da neko ne razumije'. Idiomi obično ne mijenjaju svoju strukturu (ne kaže se 'praviti se Francuz' s istim značenjem), a njihovo poznavanje i pravilna upotreba znak su gotovo izvornog vladanja jezikom.
